sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203], while operating income grew 12.3% a year and net income 14.7% [F204][F205].
The window is a steady compounder rather than a cycle: revenue growth ran between 5.0% and 17.5% every year, with the step change in FY2021 and FY2022 [D336][D189][D238].
FY2021 net sales rose 17.5% on a 16% comparable sales increase, strong non-foods and e-commerce, and gasoline price and volume recovery [D189][P56][P55].
FY2022 added 15.8% as comparable sales rose 14%, led by gasoline, business centers and travel, with inflation higher than prior years [D238][P42].
The US segment supplied +7.2pp of FY2026's 10.1% revenue growth on a 72.5% revenue share [D672][D670][D434], with Other International adding +1.6pp and Canada +1.3pp [D679][D686].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, or 10%, mainly on an 8% comparable sales increase from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency, plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].

Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue but contributed only +2.6pp of FY2026 growth, while warehouse ancillary and other businesses contributed +3.7pp on a 20.2% share [D558][D560][D601][D599].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026, an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457], and operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue [D458].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% against 13.9% net income growth as the diluted share count slipped 0.1% [D438][D436][D452].
The FY2026 operating margin of 3.9% is the window high, above the 3.4% median and the 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690], yet it sits below the 5.0% retail peer median [D710].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp: cost of revenue was flat at -0.0pp and SG&A added +0.1pp [D447][D459][D460].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of net sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency adding $126 million of expense [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.9pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap of 0.9pp [F52][F32][D448], with a 24.7% effective tax rate [D420].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income [F82][F42][D421], and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x net income, above the 0.99x window median [F102][D422][D701].

The operating cash flow increase to $15.8 billion from $13.3 billion came primarily from higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories, helped by faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [F82][F81][P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% against a 2.8% window median [D418][D698], with capex at 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [D417][D423].
Stock-based compensation was 5.8% of operating cash flow, down from 7.6% in FY2017 [D424][D12].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, in FY2026 [D427][D428], up from $9.5 billion in FY2025 [D378], with total debt of $6.2 billion [D426].

That 5.0% net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of six retail peers against a -4.4% peer median [D428][D715][D716], and the current ratio of 1.06x is above the 1.02x window median [F182][D704].
Financing used $3.4 billion, mainly dividends, buybacks and debt repayment [F122][P4], while investing used $6.4 billion, primarily capital expenditures [F112][P5].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow [D429][D430], and the share count was flat, so EPS growth tracked net income [D452].

No red-flag candidates were supplied in the pack, and the screens for margin erosion, cash conversion and leverage show none triggered: the operating margin is at its window high [F32][D691] and net cash is positive [D427].
The one structural softness is profitability against peers: the operating margin sits at the 17th percentile of six retail peers [D709], a membership-model trade-off rather than a deterioration.
If the FY2027 operating margin falls below the 3.4% window median [D692], the margin expansion described above would be reversing; it will appear in the FY2027 10-K.
If free cash flow per dollar of net income drops below the 0.99x window median [D701], the FY2026 conversion of 1.02x [D422] would be unwinding; it will appear in the FY2027 10-K cash flow statement.
If net cash as a share of revenue falls below the 3.5% FY2025 level [D379], the FY2026 build to 5.0% [D428] would be reversing; it will appear in the FY2027 10-K balance sheet.
